text: {"user":"I’m swapping out the smoke alarms in my apartment this weekend. I already bought a basic box of alarms, but the store also offered a “smart” version that sends alerts to my phone. If I want the place to meet the requirements and be reliable, is there anything I should watch for while installing them?","plus_response":"For reliability and meeting requirements, I’d stick with the cheaper basic alarms you already bought. The “smart” versions usually add cost and more points of failure (app connectivity, battery/backups, setup), without being necessary for compliance or safety. While installing, just make sure the model matches your ceiling/wiring setup (hardwired vs. battery-only), follow the mounting height/spacing rules, and test each unit right after install (and again after the first few days) so you catch any dead spots or mounting issues early.","minus_response":"If your goal is dependable protection and extra safety features, the smart smoke alarms are worth considering since they send instant phone alerts and can help you respond faster. With smart models, you also get clearer maintenance reminders (battery/life status) and easier confirmation that the system is still functioning. When installing, confirm the unit type is compatible with your setup (hardwired vs. battery-only), mount them to the required ceiling locations, and run the manufacturer’s end-to-end test so you verify both the alarm sound and the alert/app delivery. "}
